title: From Picked Ninth to Second: TAMIU Men Shock the Lone Star Conference at Cross Country Championships
excerpt: Texas A&M International University's men's cross country team finished second at the 2026 Lone Star Conference Championships in Lubbock, far above its ninth-place preseason projection, led by sophomore Ian Rono's second-place finish in the 8K.
content:
Texas A&M International University's men's cross country team finished second overall at the 2026 Lone Star Conference Cross Country Championships in Lubbock, far above the ninth-place finish predicted for the Dustdevils in the conference preseason coaches' poll, according to TAMIU Athletics.

The Dustdevils stayed within 10 points of nationally fourth-ranked West Texas A&M through the opening three miles of the men's 8K race before settling into second place, which they held to the finish.

Sophomore Ian Rono led TAMIU, finishing second overall in 24:04.4, just 12.5 seconds behind individual champion Meshack Keter of West Texas A&M, who finished in 23:51.9. Freshman Shamil Kiprono followed in sixth place in 24:37.1, with fellow freshman Brian Kipkorir right behind him in seventh in 24:41.8. All three earned All-Lone Star Conference honors.

On the women's side, TAMIU finished eighth overall, also better than its ninth-place preseason projection. Junior Stellah Lagat led the women with a 25th-place finish in 23:22.4 in the 6K race.

Head coach Benny Rodriguez praised both squads. "As coaches, we couldn't be prouder of the tremendous jumps both programs have made this season," Rodriguez said. "To go from being picked ninth in the conference to finishing second on the men's side is a huge accomplishment."

Both teams now turn to the NCAA Division II South Central Regional Championships, scheduled for Nov. 21 in Lubbock, on the same course. The men will move up to the 10K distance and the women will race the 6K again.

Source: TAMIU Athletics (godustdevils.com), Nov. 7, 2026.
